## CONTEXT
- Nxeon sells VPS + one-click game servers (Minecraft Java/Bedrock, Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2, Terraria and more), on NVMe hardware in Singapore, with full root, mod support, dedicated-IP option, and instant deploy.
- Prisma model (client already generated): `BlogPost { slug(unique), title, excerpt, body(markdown), coverEmoji, tags(String[]), author, category, published(Boolean), publishedAt(DateTime), seoTitle, seoDescription, createdAt, updatedAt }`.
- The blog renderer supports markdown: `#`/`##`/`###` headings, `**bold**`, `` `code` ``, fenced code blocks, `-` and `1.` lists, [links](url), paragraphs. Write bodies in that markdown.

## YOUR TASK
Write **30 original blog posts** covering game-server topics people actually search for. Mix these types:
- How-to guides: "How to set up a [game] server" for Minecraft (Java + Bedrock separately), Valheim, Rust, Palworld, CS2, Terraria, ARK: Survival Ascended, 7 Days to Die, Project Zomboid, Satisfactory, Factorio, Enshrouded, V Rising.
- Optimization/ops: reduce Minecraft server lag, best plugins/mods, backups, DDoS protection for game servers, how much RAM/CPU a game server needs, choosing server location/latency, modpack hosting.
- Buyer-intent: "VPS vs dedicated game server host", "how much does it cost to run a [game] server", "best VPS specs for [game]".
Each post: 600–900 words of genuinely useful, ORIGINAL content (do NOT copy text from any website/wiki — write it yourself, accurate and practical). Include real, sensible commands where relevant. Naturally reference deploying on Nxeon (one-click, NVMe, full root) without being spammy — keep it helpful first. Each must have: a keyword-focused `title`, a URL-safe `slug` (prefix game/topic, e.g. `how-to-set-up-a-minecraft-server`), a compelling 140–160 char `seoDescription`, a punchy `excerpt` (~160 chars), 3–6 `tags`, `category: "Gaming"`, a relevant `coverEmoji`, `author: "Nxeon"`, `published: true`, and a `publishedAt` you set (stagger dates across the past ~90 days using explicit `new Date("2026-05-...")` values — do NOT use `Date.now()`).

## OWNED FILE (create ONLY this)
- `prisma/seed-blog-gaming.ts` — an idempotent seeder: an array of ~30 post objects, upserting by `slug` (`db.blogPost.upsert({ where:{slug}, update:{...}, create:{...} })`). End with a console.log count. Then RUN it: `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx prisma/seed-blog-gaming.ts` (writing content rows is allowed).

## HARD RULES
- Touch ONLY `prisma/seed-blog-gaming.ts`. Do NOT edit schema, app code, other seed files, or anything else. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `prisma db push/migrate/generate`, or restart services. Do NOT git commit/push. No new npm deps.
- Content must be ORIGINAL and accurate — never reproduce copyrighted text; write everything yourself. Keep game names factual; do not fabricate fake benchmarks or false claims.
- Slugs must be unique within your file; use a distinct gaming/how-to slug namespace so you won't collide with other clusters.

## FINAL REPORT
How many posts you wrote + seeded (confirm the tsx run succeeded and the total `BlogPost` count it printed), the slug list, and anything incomplete.

Guard against this with \`StartLimitBurst\` and \`StartLimitIntervalSec\` in the \`[Unit]\` section, which stop the service after too many rapid failures so you can investigate rather than hammering a broken server. When a service goes into that state, \`journalctl -u minecraft\` shows you exactly why it's failing to boot.
